newsitem.title: IRAN: Iranian oilfield awarded to Canadian, UK firms.
newsitem.headline: Iranian oilfield awarded to Canadian, UK firms.

text.p: Iran has approved a contract giving the green light for a Canadian-British venture to develop one of its untapped offshore oilfields, a senior source at the National Iranian Oil Company (NIOC) said on Friday.

NIOC's board of directors had approved the contract for the Balal oilfield to Canadian energy independent Bow Valley and the privately owned U.K. Pell Frischmann Engineering Limited, the source told Reuters on the sidelines of an energy conference in Isfahan.
"The NIOC board recently approved the contract," the source said.
Industry sources said financing for the deal had yet to be arranged.
If that were secured and the deal signed, the Balal development would be the second project Iran has awarded to foreign firms under its "buy-back" formula that aims to boost Iran's oil capacity.

France's Total became the first foreign oil firm to secure a stake in an Iranian oilfield since the country's 1979 revolution when it signed a groundbreaking $600 million deal in July 1995 to develop Iran's Sirri fields.

That deal accelerated moves in Washington to seek ways to deter foreign investments in the Islanmic republic's oil and gas sectors which are the backbone of the country's economy and make Iran the world's third largest oil exporter.

This culminated in U.S. President Bill Clinton signing the Iran-Libya sanctions act last year which gave him power to use a wide-range of sanctions against non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more a year in the two countries' oil and gas sectors.
Washington has not reacted to energy investment deals signed by NIOC since the sanctions act came into law.

Malaysia's national oil firm Petronas has joined Total in developing the Sirri E and A oil and gas fields and Tehran has secured a $23 billion long-term supply agreement to export gas to Turkey without U.S. penalties.
The value of the proposed Balal contract was not immediately known though industry sources said the project's total cost would run up to $150 million.
Balal, located southwest of the Iranian island of Lavan, had recoverable reserves of 80 million barrels and could produce between 35,000 and 40,000 barrels per day (bpd).
Iran currently produces an average of 3.6 million bpd, but its onshore fields, which account for the vast source of output are on the maturing and are expected to steadily decline.
Under the original "buy-back" formula, Bow Valley and Pell Frischmann would receive a return on their investments by lifting crude oil from the contracted field.

NIOC offered 11 major "buy-back" projects worth some $6 billion to foreign and local firms in 1995 -- representing the biggest foreign investment opportunity in the country since the Iranian revolution.
